blocks.text: On Monday, November 16th, Gros & Delettrez auction house devotes an entire sale to Jean-Pierre Laffont, one of the great witnesses of America from the 1960s to the 1980s. More than 150 prints trace the struggles of the era, from the civil rights marches and the protests against the Vietnam War to the fall of Richard Nixon. The photographer, now 91, will be in Paris for the occasion, at the moment his new book, Rebels with a Cause (Damiani), is published, in the year of the 250th anniversary of the United States.
Auction on Monday November 16th 2026 at 2.00 pm
Viewing from November 12th to 14th, during Paris Photo · Gros & Delettrez, 2 rue de Bérite, Paris 75006

5 KEY POINTS • A monographic sale. Over 150 prints by French photojournalist Jean-Pierre Laffont, a leading figure at the Gamma and Sygma agencies, who has been based in New York since 1964. • Images that have become historic. Martin Luther King protesting against the Vietnam War (1967), Richard Nixon’s resignation (1974), Muhammad Ali (1974), the World Trade Centre (1976). • Exhibition prints. Those from his retrospective at the Maison européenne de la photographie (2015) and from Visa pour l’Image (2025). • The artist in Paris. Aged 91, he will attend the sale and sign copies of his new book, *Rebels with a Cause* (Damiani), at Paris Photo on 13 November. • A timely auction. The year of the 250th anniversary of the United States, thirteen days after the mid-term elections. Auction: Monday 16th of November 2026 at 2.00 pm Public viewing: Thursday 12th, Friday 13th and Saturday 14th of November Venue: Gros & Delettrez, 2 rue de Bérite, 75006 Paris Expert: Romain Lacroix-Nahmias Bidding: in the auction room, by telephone, by proxy and online via Drouot Live, Interenchères and Invaluable Signing of *Rebels with a Cause*: Friday November 13th at 6.00 pm, Paris Photo, Grand Palais, Damiani stand
